title: Podman should not obsess over using systemd by default on systemd systems.
body:
### Feature request description

I recently decided to switch from Docker to Podman as I find the daemonless approach very enticing.
I am running Podman on Debian 13, which uses systemd by default.
With the recent controversy regarding systemd (which is **not** the point of this request), I am considering moving from systemd to another boot manager.
When using Podman, even when telling Podman to use cgroupsf, it keeps obsessing about systemd regularly.
For example, running a simple Stalwart container will produce the following error:
```
ERRO[0000] failed to move the rootless netns pasta process to the systemd user.slice: dial unix /run/user/0/bus: connect: permission denied 
```
I understand this error, but Podman is a container runner, it should not obsess over using a boot manager as orchestrator by default.

### Suggest potential solution

Podman should avoid trying to obsessively rely on systemd when installed on a systemd system.
It should be an opt-in instead of an opt-out. If it has to stay opt-out, then the opt-out should not require such a painful process of untangling every single configuration out of systemd.

### Have you considered any alternatives?

I understand why some people would want to use systemd. I think it is also understandable why other people would not want to use systemd.

### Additional context

A few reasons why I do not want to use systemd aside from the controversy:
- systemd is not a container orchestrator, it's not designed for this, it's not its responsibility.
- managing all container logs through journald is not something I am interested in. It would require a considerable machinery and a lot of engineering for something that is already trivially solved using a normal container orchestration.
- I do not want any non administrator manipulating systemctl.
